This project will investigate the sorption of MeSe(IV) and DMSeO onto iron (Fe) and manganese (Mn) oxides, which are ubiquitous minerals in the environment and important substrate for attenuation of many metals. Currently, there is no literature on this process, forming an important knowledge gap on the transport of Se species in the environment. 825497.area: Environmental impact of economic activities (including agriculture)
825497.subject: Environmental geology
825497.summary: Throughout Canada and globally groundwater resources are under continuous threat from industry and other anthropogenic activities. The protection of this resource is vital for the health of humans and ecosystems, and economic security. Canada's economy relies heavily on the resource sector, but these activities, due to their nature and scale have significant impact on the environment. For example, mining operations, including mineral and petroleum resources, generate waste products that have potential to leach contaminant, and particularly toxic metals, into the environment. The transport and fate of contaminants in groundwater and in soils often involve complex biogeochemical reactions coupled to physical transport and attenuation processes. 830151.subject: Economic geology
830151.summary: Summary of Proposal As the global economy grows to match the anticipated level of prosperity of the world's peak population, that the global primary metal production is predicted to at least double by 2060. Several key commodities like nickel may see up to 20-fold increases in demand as the economy moves toward full electrification. Currently recognized resources of nickel and several other important metals will fall far short of expected demand. Supply shortfalls will cause a surge in exploration for conventional mineral deposit types as well as increased scrutiny of mineralization styles currently regarded as being subeconomic. 830153.subject: Environmental geology
830153.summary: The boreal biome in Alberta is a vast, ecologically diverse region spanning the northern part of the province. Three percent of the region comprises lakes that support abundant aquatic life. These lakes are of great importance to the economic and cultural well-being of the people living there. Many lakes in the region face environmental challenges related to high levels of nutrient enrichment (eutrophication) from agriculture, industry, and/or municipalities, as well as the effects of a variable and rapidly changing climate. Fully understanding the degree to which lake eutrophication is driven by climate change is hampered by the short instrumental climatological record. 827108.subject: Biostatistics
827108.summary: Mixture models continue to be the most popular approach for learning hidden cluster structure in heterogenous data. Mixture-based cluster analysis assumes that data arise from a mixture of homogenous subpopulations where a cluster can be modeled parametrically via a component density. In model-based clustering (unsupervised) as opposed to model-based classification (semi-supervised), no group label information is available for any observations. Advantages of probabilistic mixture model clustering as well as the statistical grounding for such models is well established. The long term goal of the applicant's research program is to develop flexible statistical models for biological and clinical data sets to gain deeper insight into complex underlying processes. 830152.subject: Cell differentiation
830152.summary: The epithelial lining of our intestine rapidly turns over, completely replaced every week, and fueled by adult intestinal stem cells. Intestinal stem cells divide daily and give rise to all intestinal epithelial lineages including absorptive enterocytes, mucus-producing goblet cells, and antimicrobial-secreting Paneth cells. In contrast, during the fetal stage, there is no such hierarchy, and virtually any cell can be the clonal origin for large patches of tissue. Postnatally, a switch occurs from this fetal non-hierarchal system to the adult stem-cell based system, via an unknown mechanism. Organoids are 3-dimensional organ-like structures cultured in petri dishes that mimic their in vivo counterparts. 823762.subject: Bacteriology
823762.summary: Bacteria are able to survive under a variety of often harmful environmental conditions such as heat or cold, nutrient limitation, low ph or antimicrobial treatment due to a multitude of adaptation processes and stress responses. One important adaptation and survival strategy exhibited by a wide range of bacteria is the formation of biofilms. Biofilms are communities of microorganisms attached to a surface and embedded in a self-produced, polymeric matrix. Biofilm bacteria have been shown to possess unique characteristics including increased stress resistance and higher antimicrobial tolerance leading to failures in bacterial eradication in many technical settings including drinking and waste water industries. 827318.subject: Aquatic ecology and limnology
827318.summary: Human activities are having a profound impact on aquatic ecosystems degrading water quality and reducing biodiversity. In fact, lakes and rivers are some of the most impacted ecosystems on the planet and there is a growing need to understand how human actions are altering these environments, particularly over longer time scales (decades or longer) where data are scarce. This proposed program will employ both paleoecological techniques and modern sampling to investigate how human actions are altering lake ecosystems, with special focus on the highly biodiverse and productive nearshore environment (littoral zone). 831785.subject: Statistics and probability
831785.summary: This research proposal aims to better understand travel times on transportation networks by modelling them as a continuous process that changes over space and time. This approach is more complex than current methods that only calculate a point estimate, namely the expected time of arrival. The research will explore the theoretical properties of these processes and then apply the findings to develop better tools for the transportation industry. The research is important because it can lead to more efficient and reliable transportation systems. This is beneficial for a wide range of people, including transportation professionals, ride-share providers, routing and logistic services, policymakers, researchers, and everyday Canadians. 828610.summary: In 1925 our view of the physical world drastically changed with the advent of Heisenberg's matrix mechanics, wherein quantum phenomena are accurately described by non-commuting operators rather than functions. This ``quantization'' of functions, which underlies the theoretical development of quantum mechanics, has motivated the quantization of other areas of mathematics, including functional analysis, group theory and information theory. The resulting areas, operator algebras, quantum groups and quantum information, have profound structure theories, and deep mathematical connections between them continue to emerge. 825502.subject: Biostatistics
825502.summary: Identification and analysis of population heterogeneity is the primary goal of cluster analysis. Clustering allows us to summarize data into homogenous groups or clusters of observations where observations within each cluster are more similar than between clusters. Model-based clustering, which utilizes mixture models, has been increasingly used in the last two decades. A finite mixture model assumes that the population consists of a finite mixture of subpopulations or components, each of which can be represented by a parametric model. Depending on the nature of the data, appropriate distributions are chosen to model various kinds of data. 825515.subject: Operator algebra
825515.summary: Von Neumann introduced operator algebras to express quantum mechanics in a mathematical language. C*-algebras are a tractable and rich class of operator algebras, and their study has a geometric flavour---they have been described by Connes as "noncommutative geometry". Geometry is governed by its beautiful symmetries, and my program explores the extent to which C*-algebras are governed by "partial symmetries" through structures called groupoids and inverse semigroups. A groupoid is certain type of set of partial symmetries on some geometric space. To every groupoid, one may construct a C*-algebra built from it. 828343.subject: Statistics and probability
828343.summary: One of the key problems in quantitative risk management is to assess various types of risks with available data and their implications in decision-making. The long--term goal of the research program is to develop statistical methods and provide implementation schemes for insurance companies, banks, and regulators to better manage risks. In this proposal, the objective is to advance the theory and applications of risk functionals. The detailed objectives are listed as follows. First, while most existing works study the statistical methods of the industry benchmarks Value--at--Risk and Expected--Shortfall, we focus on developing statistical methods of the general class of risk functionals in insurance and finance, including variability measures and risk functionals in higher--dimensions. 830138.subject: Pure mathematics
830138.summary: Algebraic geometry is the study of solution spaces of polynomials in several variables. This includes the geometry of familiar shapes like parabolas, spheres, and curves in the plane defined by a polynomial. One tries to study the solutions by relating them to other spaces via mappings or parametrizations. This subject is highly controlled by the algebra of polynomials. Geometric statements about the space of solutions correspond directly to algebraic statements about the polynomial equations one is solving. In noncommutative algebra, applying operations in different orders can yield different results. We have that x times y is not necessarily equal to y times x. Noncommutative algebra, just as in the study of the algebra of polynomials, is often motivated by geometric problems and intuition. 827126.subject: Operations research and management science
827126.summary: In recent years, the proliferation of technologies, easier access to big data, wide introduction of cloud storage and computing, and exponential growth of the Internet, wireless and smartphone apps have profoundly impacted everybody's daily life. These advancements and their subsequent impacts have created many new challenges, which in turn greatly motivate research on large-scale complex systems, multi-dimensional networks, adaptive models, parallel processing, and cloud computing. Many of the new challenges cannot be satisfactorily addressed by classical or standard methods, which call for new innovative mathematical/statistical modeling and solution methodologies. 831575.subject: Algebra
831575.summary: The focus of this research project is the theory of AV-modules, which sits at the intersection of algebraic geometry and non-commutative algebra. AV-modules are structures that admit compatible actions of both the Lie algebra of vector fields and the commutative algebra of functions. While some AV-modules have clear geometric origins, recent developments have uncovered new, exotic modules within this framework. The theory of AV-modules can be seen as an extension of the highly successful theory of D-modules, which describes modules over the algebra of differential operators. In addition to my work on AV-modules, I am also engaged in applied problems within Data Science. Recently, I developed a novel algorithm for identifying the densest subgraph in large hypergraphs. 830146.subject: Pure mathematics
830146.summary: The oldest questions in mathematics are questions about the relationships between whole numbers--for example finding patterns among all of the prime numbers. Despite their superficial simplicity, questions about numbers can be very difficult to answer, and so an enormous amount of theory has been built up to help find answers. One of the discoveries in the late twentieth century was that information about numbers could be packaged into mathematical objects that usually describe the symmetries of some classical geometric spaces. I am trying to determine just what kind of information is packaged in precisely what manner. This is important to a large number of mathematicians internationally, because it reveals a new structure that numbers possess. Canadians benefit in this research as it connects us to a continuing global endeavour to understand numbers better.

831459.summary: My research encompasses two primary areas: the study of partial differential equations (PDEs) with an emphasis on the calculus of variations, and the theory and applications of optimal mass transportation. The calculus of variations stands out as one of the most powerful and versatile methodologies for enhancing our understanding of mathematics and its practical implications. In contemporary mathematical sciences, researchers are actively engaged in addressing a myriad of problems modeled by PDEs. This research is particularly vital in applied physics, mathematical modeling, and engineering disciplines. 830150.subject: Mathematics of computing
830150.summary: The focus of this research proposal is on the theory and real-world applications of finite fields. These algebraic objects have a long history in mathematics. The theory, applications and algorithms of finite fields have become central to countless areas in communications and security. In particular, they play a central role in cryptography and coding theory. Our plan has four axes of research: (a) the study of iterations of functions over finite fields; (b) the development of algorithms for operations involving polynomials over finite fields in use in post-quantum cryptography (PQC); (c) the construction of efficient codes; and (d) the creation of combinatorial arrays built from finite field theory. 827115.subject: Biostatistics
827115.summary: In clinical studies, we often encounter multivariate data featuring many complex issues including frailties in survival outcomes, correlations in longitudinal outcomes, left-censoring in biomarkers, measurement errors in covariates, and outliers in response variables. Joint modeling of longitudinal and survival data is often used when the focus is on the survival times of individuals and one wishes to study the effect of endogenous time-dependent covariates or biomarkers on the survival times. Often values of a clinical covariate or biomarker are unobserved but known to be below a threshold called the limit of detection (LOD). 830157.subject: Statistics and probability
830157.summary: The last three decades have seen the development of statistical models that are infinite (or 'high') dimensional. The main target of statistical inference in high-dimensional models is a function or an infinite vector. In view of modern computational techniques, such models are tractable and attractive in statistical practice. The goal of this research project is to elaborate statistically efficient and computationally feasible methods that would allow scientists and practitioners to make statistical inference in sparse high-dimensional models and apply the proposed methods for analyzing real-life data. 828339.subject: Combinatorics
828339.summary: I am interested in the mathematical theory and real world application of finite set systems. I propose research on generalizations of orthogonal arrays which are two-dimensional arrays of symbols with the property that when some small sets of columns are extracted, the resulting rows contain every possible vector with some uniformity. They have applications to numerical methods, software testing, and optimized welding design. Orthogonal arrays (OA) require all small sets of columns and every possible row must appear the same number of times. I am proposing two generalizations, poset OAs where the selection of columns is restricted to the ideals of a partially ordered sets and Lee OAs where all sets of columns are selected but which do not require that all vectors appear. 827134.subject: Neurophysiology
827134.summary: In mice, like most mammals, social behaviours increase survival and reproductive fitness. Social memory is a core element of social interaction, allowing recognition of stranger and familiar individuals. The CA2 subregion of the hippocampus is a crucial hub for encoding social memory and the control of social aggression. The role of CA2 in social memory has only been investigated in male mice; thus, it is unclear whether sex differences exist. Other forms of hippocampal-mediated memory (i.e., spatial memory) depend on the induction of gene transcription and mRNA translation of proteins that are just beginning to be identified. However, the molecular underpinnings of CA2-mediated social memory encoding remain poorly understood. 829357.subject: Animal physiology and metabolism
829357.summary: Energy regulation is essential for life and balances the energy demands of an organism with food availability. Prolonged periods where energy demands exceed food intake would lead to starvation and eventually death. Paradoxically, while energy balance is needed for survival, it is also dependent on motivated actions like going to look for food and then moving towards the food source. This locomotor or activity aspect of energy balance is considerably less studied than feeding. This Discovery Grant aims to investigate the brain processes that regulate motivated activity to regulate energy balance. Melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH) is one important peptide hormone whose actions promote energy storage. 827112.subject: Life sciences research related to human health and disease
827112.summary: Sex hormones, such as estrogen, progesterone and testosterone have widespread influences on cognition, affective states, and stress reactivity. Indeed, fluctuations of sex hormones across the menstrual cycle correspond to altered brain activity and connectivity, alterations in stress hormones, such as cortisol, and pro-inflammatory cytokines (i.e., signaling molecules released by immune cells). Although there has been a shift in the past 10 years to include females in biological research, sex is most often not the focus of the investigation. As a result, significant gaps remain in our understanding as to how alterations in sex hormones, for example through the menstrual cycle or use of hormonal contraceptives, affects biological stress responses in females. 827114.subject: Inter-cellular communication
827114.summary: Sex differences exist from neuroanatomy to behaviour. As such, characterising sex differences in the building of neural systems over development is essential to understanding the contributions of sex to systems level neuroscience in adult brain functions. A great deal of research has identified astroglial cells as critical players in all central nervous system functions, including in the development and maintenance of neurons and neuronal networks. Given the involvement of astroglial cells in neuronal network function, it is perhaps not surprising that astroglial cells also show sex differences in morphology, gene/protein expression patterns and functions. 823533.summary: The optimal functioning of the nervous system involves proper activity-dependent refinement of neuronal circuits during critical periods (CPs) in early life. Such periods are characterized by highest level of synaptic plasticity, rapid learning, synaptogenesis as well as enduring consequences for neuronal connectivity. Currently, the cellular and molecular mechanisms of CP plasticity remain elusive, although the prevailing notion is that the finely tuned local excitatory/inhibitory balance determines the CP plasticity. The maturation of inhibition from parvalbumin-positive inhibitory interneuron has been implicated in the formation of CPs for sensory plasticity. 828333.subject: Behavioural neuroscience --learning
828333.summary: The current proposal is based on the idea that multiple brain regions interact over time to store memories and that changes in the relationships between and within the cellular components of these networks serve to represent long-term memory and preserve memory function over the lifespan. We will investigate the development of hippocampal-cortical circuits by manipulating the external environmental configuration or the internal neurogenic environment and assessing long-term outcomes on cognitive and social behaviors. The aim is to broaden the scope of our understanding of how alterations in the external and internal environments during postnatal development can affect the stability of memories over the lifespan. 827105.subject: Biological and Medical Physics
827105.summary: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has revolutionized human neurosciences by providing a non-invasive tool for dynamically mapping brain activity without the use of ionizing radiation or exogenous contrast agents. Most fMRI studies exploit the Blood Oxygenation Level-Dependent (BOLD) effect, whereby the oxygen saturation of blood modulates the MRI signal level, to localize changes in blood oxygenation that are related to changing neuronal activity. 828332.subject: Physics
828332.summary: Approximately half of all cancer treatments in Canada employ radiation therapy. These treatments are delivered in multiple treatment sessions over a timespan of weeks. Accurate delivery of the prescribed radiation dose is required to preserve the balance between tumour control and normal tissue toxicity. However, a patient's anatomy varies over the timespan of a single treatment, due to physiological processes such as respiration, as well as over the timespan of a treatment course, due to tumour regression/progression and normal tissue response to radiation. A proposed solution to this problem is adaptive radiation therapy, which adjusts the treatment plan to compensate for the anatomical changes detected at the time of treatment. 830158.subject: Biological and Medical Physics
830158.summary: Radiation medicine plays a critical role in the lives of many Canadians for diagnosis and treatment, e.g., with 1 in 4 undergoing cancer radiation therapy in their lifetime. All radiation treatments aim to maximize tumour cell kill while limiting healthy tissue exposure; the figure of merit is typically "absorbed dose" which is the energy deposited per unit mass of tissue and is evaluated by physicists. Despite the ubiquity of radiation medicine, fundamental scientific questions remain regarding the interactions of radiation with matter, radiation dosimetry, and biological effects of radiation. Advances in radiation medicine require new approaches for evaluating energy deposition (dose) and connecting with biological response across length and complexity scales ranging from cellular to patient systems. 827113.summary: Radiation therapy (RT) is a standard treatment for ~50% of cancers worldwide. Radiation protection (RP) aims to ensure public health safety from exposure to ionizing radiation (IR) arising from all sources including RT. Major goals in RT and RP require new tools for improved mechanistic understanding of radiobiological response, and for high precision IR dosimetry.
